Article Title: EPFO has an official WhatsApp channel for PF updates; here’s how to join and get educational information on EPF advance withdrawals and more
Article Text:
Besides sharing updates, the EPFO WhatsApp channel also provides members with educational content.

How to join EPFO WhatsApp channel

Information on EPF advance withdrawals

Details of the Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana

Information on EPF contributions after rejoining employment

Other EPFO awareness and service-related videos

Many banks offer WhatsApp services

How EPF WhatsApp service will work

Simpler withdrawal rules

Auto settlement limits

The Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) has been taking steps to keep members informed and allow access for more information digitally. As part of this effort, the retirement fund body has asked members to follow its official WhatsApp channel for the latest updates and useful information concerning their provident fund accounts.The EPFO, in a social media post on X (formerly Twitter), said that members who join the WhatsApp channel can stay informed about the organisation’s latest updates.In its post on X, the EPFO said, “Join EPFO's official WhatsApp Channel to get important updates and useful information. Click on the link to join.”Members can access the official EPFO WhatsApp channel by using the link provided by the organisation.Members can join the EPFO’s official WhatsApp channel through the following link: https://www.whatsapp.com/channel/0029Vb6kmH48Pgs8ftd6Kw3YBesides sharing updates, the EPFO WhatsApp channel also provides members with educational content through useful links. These include YouTube videos covering topics such as EPF advance withdrawals, EPF contributions after an employee rejoins employment and the payment process under the Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana.Types of educational links shared by the EPFO on WhatsAppThe EPFO’s official website provides members with information about several services, including EPF Advance, EPF withdrawal, UAN activation, claims and transfers, KYC, and pension-related facilities.The EPF scheme provides retirement savings along with tax-free interest growth, contributions from the employer and financial security for the family. Among its key features are a 12% contribution rate, online access to the EPF passbook, convenient transfer of accounts, nomination facilities and options to withdraw funds.Several banks in India have introduced WhatsApp-based services through which customers can securely perform tasks such as checking account balances, downloading statements, managing cards and requesting various services at any time. To use these facilities, customers generally need to send a 'Hi' from the mobile number registered with their bank.In May, the Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) was reportedly working on plans to introduce its services through WhatsApp.A PTI report, citing Labour Minister Mansukh Mandaviya, said the EPFO intended to use WhatsApp because of the messaging platform’s widespread use among mobile phone users across the country.Under the proposed system, EPFO members would be able to initiate a conversation with the organisation by sending a 'Hello' message to its verified WhatsApp number, which would carry a green tick.Members would also be able to receive updates related to the EPFO directly on their registered mobile numbers. According to the report, the service would support local and regional languages, allowing users to communicate in a language they are more comfortable with.Earlier this year, EPFO streamlined its partial PF withdrawal framework by consolidating 13 separate provisions into three broad categories: Essential Needs, Housing Needs and Special Circumstances.Under the revised rules, members can withdraw up to 100% of their eligible PF balance, while the withdrawal limits for education and marriage have also been increased. The minimum service requirement has been reduced to 12 months.Another key change is that members can seek a withdrawal under the ‘Special Circumstances’ category without having to provide a reason. The reform is intended to enable 100% auto-settlement of eligible claims, while keeping 25% of the PF balance invested for retirement.At present, members have to submit withdrawal applications, which can sometimes result in delays. With the auto-settlement facility, however, eligible withdrawal claims are processed electronically without manual intervention. Once the application is filed, subscribers can receive the money within three days.The EPFO has also raised the limit under the auto-settlement facility to Rs 5 lakh from Rs 1 lakh. The facility allows subscribers to access their funds within three days for requirements including marriage, education, illness and housing.
Article Summary: The Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) has been taking steps to keep members informed and allow access for more information digitally. As part of this effort, the retirement fund body has asked members to follow its official WhatsApp channel for the latest updates and useful information.

Article Title: UPI payments up to Rs 2,000 to remain free of charges: Govt
Article Text:
UPI payments. (Representative image)

Government on Monday notified that banks and payment system providers cannot impose direct or indirect charges on Unified Payments Interface (UPI) transactions of up to Rs 2,000 or payments made using RuPay debit cards.The notification was issued under Section 10A of the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007.“In exercise of the powers conferred by section 10 A of the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007 (51 of 2007), the Central Government hereby specifies the following electronic modes of payment, namely: (i) Debit Card powered by RuPay; and (ii) Unified Payments Interface (UPI) transactions upto Rs. 2,000,” the ministry of finance said.“No bank or system provider shall impose, whether directly or indirectly, any charge upon a person making or receiving a payment by using the electronic modes of payment specified in paragraph above,” it added.The notification keeps UPI transactions of up to Rs 2,000 free of charges and paves the way for a possible nominal Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) on selected UPI merchant transactions above a specified threshold.The government had indicated in August that consumers and person-to-person payments would continue to remain free. Any fee, if introduced, would be paid by merchants rather than consumers, government officials said, according to Reuters.The government said the proposed changes were part of a broader effort to make India’s digital payments ecosystem sustainable, competitive and capable of supporting the country’s growing digital economy.The finance ministry also rejected reports that external influences were behind the proposed policy changes, describing such claims as “unfounded, completely false and misleading.”Launched a decade ago, UPI processed 24.51 billion transactions worth Rs 29.82 trillion in August. Google Pay and Walmart-owned PhonePe accounted for around three-fourths of the month’s total UPI transaction volume.
Article Summary: Government on Monday notified that banks and payment system providers cannot impose direct or indirect charges on Unified Payments Interface (UPI) transactions of up to Rs 2,000. The notification was issued under Section 10A of the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007. UPI processed 24.51 billion transactions worth Rs 29.82 trillion in August.

Article Title: Rishikesh-Karnprayag railway line project for Char Dham connectivity boost hits 41 tunnel breakthroughs; RVNL completes 10.847-km Escape Tunnel 1, with 5 more expected within a year
Article Text:
The completion is particularly significant given the difficult geological conditions along the Himalayan alignment. (Image for representative purpose only)

Why tunnel breakthrough is important

Rishikesh-Karnaprayag new rail line

The 125 kilometres long Rishikesh-Karnaprayag new railway line, which is currently under construction, has achieved a major milestone with a new tunnel breakthrough. Rail Vikas Nigam Limited (RVNL), which is the implementing body for the project, has completed another major milestone in the Rishikesh-Karnprayag New Broad Gauge Rail Line Project with the final breakthrough of Escape Tunnel 1. This takes the total number of tunnel breakthroughs in the project to 41.The Rishikesh Project Implementation Unit of RVNL achieved the breakthrough on Friday after completing the full 10.847-km length of Escape Tunnel 1. The tunnel is the second-longest on the project.The completion is particularly significant given the difficult geological conditions along the Himalayan alignment. The route passes through rock formations that are highly tectonized, multi-folded and extensively faulted, with widespread shearing and areas of intense rock crushing.Officials said these challenging geological conditions led to the development of thick mylonite zones, which are largely associated with the tunnel's proximity to the Main Boundary Thrust (MBT).The project has now recorded 41 tunnel breakthroughs, with work progressing towards completion. The remaining five breakthroughs are expected to be completed over the next year, taking the project closer to its final target.The latest breakthrough is being seen as another significant engineering achievement for the Rishikesh-Karnprayag rail project and brings the Himalayan railway connectivity initiative a step closer to completion.The 125-km Rishikesh-Karnaprayag new rail line has been sanctioned to provide rail connectivity for the Chardham pilgrimage circuit.The project runs through Dehradun, Tehri Garhwal, Pauri Garhwal, Rudraprayag and Chamoli districts of Uttarakhand.It is intended to connect the religious and tourist destinations of Devprayag and Karnaprayag with Rishikesh and the National Capital of India through the railway network.A large number of pilgrims from across the country visit the Char Dhams, while Uttarakhand also draws a significant number of domestic and international tourists for trekking and sightseeing.However, the existing road network passes through fragile mountain slopes and faces major limitations in terms of traffic load, capacity, safety and speed. Providing rail connectivity to the Char Dhams will make travel safer, more economical and comfortable, while also making it more environment-friendly and reliable throughout the year.A large part of the alignment runs through tunnels. The project comprises 16 main-line tunnels covering 104 km and 12 escape tunnels extending about 98 km.As per a July 2026 update, 101 km of main-line tunnelling and more than 95 km of the nine escape tunnels have been completed.To accelerate construction, eight adits were identified at different tunnel locations. These adits provided additional faces for tunnel excavation, helping speed up work on the longer tunnels. All eight adits, covering a combined length of 5 km, have now been completed.The rail line also requires the construction of 19 important/major bridges. Eight of these 19 bridges have been completed, while work on the remaining bridges has also commenced.Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw has said that surveys have been completed for extending rail connectivity to Gangotri, Yamunotri, Kedarnath and Badrinath. However, the proposed alignment is located close to the main Central thrust of the Himalayas, an area that is highly seismically active.The timeline and cost of railway projects are influenced by several factors. These include land acquisition, forest clearance, relocation of infringing utilities, statutory approvals from different authorities, geological and topographical conditions, the law and order situation around the project site, and the number of months during which work can be carried out at a particular site each year.All these factors have a bearing on both the completion schedule and the cost of railway projects.
Article Summary: The 125-km Rishikesh-Karnaprayag new rail line has been sanctioned to provide rail connectivity for the Chardham pilgrimage circuit. The completion is particularly significant given the difficult geological conditions along the Himalayan alignment. The project comprises 16 main-line tunnels covering 104 km and 12 escape tunnels extending about 98 km.

Article Title: Oil price today: Brent crude rises as Saudi pipeline outage, fresh attacks raise supply concerns
Article Text:
The rise in oil prices added to inflation concerns.

Oil prices rose more than 1% on Tuesday as concerns over global supplies intensified after attacks disrupted Saudi Arabia’s East-West pipeline and planned talks between Gulf Arab states and Iran were postponed.Brent crude futures gained $1.24, or 1.18%, to $106.93 a barrel at 0026 GMT, after rising 1% in the previous session. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures climbed $1.29, or 1.24%, to $102.65 a barrel, following a 1.3% increase on Monday.Iran-backed Houthi forces in Yemen launched fresh attacks on Saudi Arabia on Monday, targeting the Khamis Mushait military airbase in the country’s south.The Houthis said the missile and drone attack was carried out in retaliation for Saudi strikes in Yemen. The assault reportedly targeted aircraft hangars, radar systems, runways and ammunition depots.The latest attack followed strikes on Friday that Riyadh blamed on Iran-backed fighters in Iraq. Those attacks disrupted Saudi Arabia’s East-West pipeline, which allows the kingdom to transport oil to the Red Sea and bypass the Strait of Hormuz.Saudi Arabia uses the pipeline to reroute around four million barrels of oil per day to the port of Yanbu.The outage could remove as much as 4% of global oil supply from the market if operations are not restored, according to Saudi buyers and traders.Shipping concerns also deepened after commodity vessel traffic through the Strait of Hormuz fell to fewer than 10 transits a day over the weekend, compared with a 10-day average of 14.The waterway carried nearly one-fifth of global oil supplies before the US-Israeli war on Iran began on February 28. Gulf Arab states also postponed planned discussions with Iran, adding to concerns that the regional conflict could widen and further disrupt energy shipments.The rise in oil prices added to inflation concerns and pushed benchmark 10-year US Treasury yields to 5% overnight—their highest level since October 2023. The yield later eased to 4.9895%.Asian shares remained subdued as investors assessed Middle East tensions, higher oil prices and elevated bond yields ahead of key central bank meetings in the United States and Japan.MSCI’s broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan fell 0.12%, while South Korea’s benchmark declined 0.25%. Japan’s Nikkei edged up 0.19% after recovering from early losses.The Bank of Japan is widely expected to raise its interest rate by 25 basis points to 1.25% at the end of its two-day meeting on Friday and signal further tightening.In currency markets, the dollar index rose 0.05% to 99.53. The dollar gained 0.17% against the yen to 154.61, while the euro slipped 0.03% to $1.1543. Spot gold fell 0.15% to $4,291.59 an ounce, while silver declined 0.31% to $63.03.
Article Summary: Brent crude futures gained $1.24, or 1.18%, to $106.93 a barrel at 0026 GMT. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures climbed 1.24% to $102.65 a barrel, following a 1.3% increase on Monday.

Article Title: Real estate businessman lost Rs 34.21 lakh in F&O trading; taxman called it speculative, but ITAT Delhi allowed Rs 25.09 lakh as business loss: Here’s why
Article Text:
The AO invoked the Explanation to Section 73. (Image for representative purpose only)

Why did the taxpayer win the case?

A taxpayer from Mathura earned Rs 8.64 crore through his real estate trading business. However, the said taxpayer alsoincurred a loss of around Rs 34 lakh from futures and options (F&O) trading in the stock market. When the taxpayer filed his income tax return (ITR), he reported the F&O loss as a business loss.The Income Tax Assessing Officer (AO) from I.P. Estate, New Delhi, did not allow this believing that since the taxpayer’s primary business was real estate trading rather than F&O trading, the AO treated the derivative loss as speculative in nature.The AO invoked the Explanation to Section 73 and consequently refused to allow the loss to be set off against the taxpayer’s regular business income. The assessment relied on the Delhi High Court ruling in CIT v. DLF Commercial Developers Ltd.The AO also disallowed Rs 10 lakh from the taxpayer’s overall business expenses, estimating that this portion was attributable to his share trading activities.As a result, the total disallowance connected with the taxpayer’s share and derivative transactions came to Rs 44 lakh. In addition, another disallowance of Rs 9,910 was made under Section 14A read with Rule 8D.The taxpayer challenged the assessment before the CIT(A), but the appellate authority upheld the AO’s decision. The matter was subsequently taken to the ITAT Delhi tax tribunal.The taxpayer eventually succeeded before the ITAT Delhi on July 10, 2026.Chartered Accountant Suresh Surana told ET ITAT Delhi drew a distinction between transactions involving the purchase and sale of shares and those carried out in exchange-traded derivatives.The tribunal pointed out that the deeming provision contained in the Explanation to Section 73 is specifically directed at a company whose business involves the purchase and sale of shares of other companies. According to ITAT Delhi, the provision does not specifically bring futures and options transactions within its scope.The tribunal also noted that eligible derivative transactions executed on a recognised stock exchange are excluded from the definition of a speculative transaction under Section 43(5)(d).While arriving at its conclusion, ITAT Delhi relied on the Bombay High Court ruling in Souvenir Developers (India) Pvt. Ltd. v. Union of India. That judgment had also considered the Delhi High Court’s decision in DLF Commercial Developers. Based on this, ITAT Delhi concluded that the Explanation to Section 73 could not be stretched to cover exchange-traded derivative transactions.The taxpayer had reported a total trading loss of Rs. 34,21,431. Of this, ITAT Delhi classified Rs 9,11,932, which arose from the actual purchase and sale of shares, as speculative loss. The remaining Rs 25,09,499 represented derivative losses and was treated as an ordinary business loss, making it eligible for treatment and set-off under the provisions applicable to business losses.The tribunal also found that the Assessing Officer had not established any calculation, evidence or reasonable basis for attributing Rs 10 lakh of the taxpayer’s business expenditure to share-trading activities. Since the amount had been determined merely on an estimated basis, ITAT Delhi reduced the disallowance to Rs 1 lakh, which it considered fair and reasonable in the circumstances.This brought down the total disallowance from Rs 44,21,431 to Rs 10,11,932. The amount sustained consisted of Rs. 9,11,932 towards the share-trading loss and Rs 1 lakh towards the related expenditure. The remaining addition of Rs 34,09,499 was deleted.Surana said the tribunal also removed the separate Rs 9,910 disallowance made under Section 14A. The taxpayer’s financial records showed that no exempt dividend income had been earned during the relevant year.ITAT Delhi relied on the decisions in Cheminvest Ltd. v. CIT, CIT v. Holcim India Pvt. Ltd. and South Indian Bank Ltd. v. CIT to hold that a Section 14A disallowance cannot be imposed where there is no exempt income.The central reason for the taxpayer’s success was the AO’s treatment of derivative transactions as equivalent to the purchase and sale of shares. ITAT Delhi held that the deeming fiction contained in the Explanation to Section 73 has to be applied strictly and cannot be expanded to cover exchange-traded derivatives falling under Section 43(5)(d).Surana said the taxpayer had another two reasons in his favour. The Rs 10 lakh allocation of expenses by the AO was not supported by any proper basis, while the absence of exempt income meant there was no ground for making a disallowance under Section 14A.The appeal was consequently partly allowed. The tribunal sustained only the actual share-trading loss of Rs 9,11,932 and Rs 1 lakh towards the associated expenditure, while deleting the remaining additions.
Article Summary: A taxpayer from Mathura earned Rs 8.64 crore through his real estate trading business. The taxpayer alsoincurred a loss of around Rs 34 lakh from futures and options (F&O) trading in the stock market. When the taxpayer filed his income tax return (ITR), he reported the F&O loss as a business loss.

Article Title: She returned after firms in UK refused visa sponsorship due to high costs. She is not alone, Indian professionals from US returning too, but at significantly lower salaries
Article Text:
The rising cost of hiring overseas workers is now beginning to influence the way Indian companies approach talent. (Image for representative purpose only)

Rising cost of UK Visa

Jobs in Metro Cities

Career choices

US No Different

Jobs not as high-paying in India

A 25 year-old Indian professional did not want to come back to India after completing her communications and media course in the United Kingdom in 2024. She had almost two years in which to look for employment there. But, ultimately she had no choice!What disrupted those plans was not a lack of qualifications, but the growing expense involved in getting a work visa sponsored.And she is not alone. This is a growing trend that is disrupting Indians’ UK dreams.The UK has tightened its work visa requirements at least twice over the past two years. The minimum salary threshold for positions eligible for a skilled worker visa increased from nearly $35,409 in 2024 to around $52,303 by April, before rising further to nearly $56,358 in July 2025.The rising cost of hiring overseas workers is now beginning to influence the way Indian companies approach talent that has gained experience abroad.At least two companies that considered the 25-year old professional for jobs told her that sponsoring her visa was beyond what they could afford. “They were like, you’re great, but we can’t have you. Because two years down the line, we’re not going to be able to sponsor you,” she told ETA Bengaluru-based company recently advertised for an AI/ML engineer using ‘Reverse Brain Drain’ as a catchphrase.An analysis by the financial daily of such job postings also found openings at companies including Reliance Industries, Mahindra Automotive and Axis Bank specifically aimed at people returning to India.The above-mentioned individual returned to India earlier this year after her visa expired.Another professional quoted in the report is currently searching for employment in India that offers a salary of at least 9 lakh a year.“Whatever I earn in the UK is going towards my expenses, which are too high over the years,” he said. He, however, does not want to return until he has secured a job that would enable him to repay his loans.The trend is also beginning to reflect in the employment market. Student Circus, a career platform based in the UK, enables students to search for jobs in the UK as well as other countries.Student Circus has now begun featuring job openings in India as well, and the response to these listings is increasing.The number of views for India-based jobs on the platform climbed to 22,312 by July 2026, almost three times the 8,052 views recorded in 2023.“For international students, getting the first job is only one part of the equation. The ability to secure sponsorship, build a long-term career and remain in the country increasingly factors into where they choose to start their careers,” said Tripti Maheshwari, cofounder of Student Circus, which partners with universities including Leeds, Bristol and Imperial College London.The majority of graduates searching through the platform are targeting opportunities in metro cities, particularly Bengaluru, Mumbai, Gurugram and Hyderabad.A 26-year old individual had been employed as a social work officer in London. With her visa approaching its expiry, she began considering whether returning to India would be necessary. Her employer did not offer visa sponsorship, while the UK was simultaneously making its visa requirements more stringent.“Towards the end, I think like my last six months over there, they also tightened the visa criteria,” she said.By October last year, she had stopped applying for positions in the UK and was focusing exclusively on opportunities in India. She secured a job in April this year, although several friends who returned during roughly the same period have continued to remain without employment.“I know seven-eight people who are literally unemployed right now and they’re not getting a job,” she said.The change in career plans is taking place as more people leave the UK. Data from the Office for National Statistics showed that an estimated 278,000 non-European Union nationals left the UK on a long-term basis in the year ending 2025. Indians constituted the largest nationality among those leaving, followed by Chinese nationals.The phenomenon extends beyond the UK, with immigration policies and uncertainty surrounding visas increasingly influencing the professional decisions of Indians working or studying overseas.The United States is witnessing a similar pattern, as some Indian professionals are choosing to return amid uncertainty surrounding their visas.“Returnee volumes have risen every year, and the gap between outbound and returning talent continues to narrow. H-1B policy is one factor, with the new petition fee and shifting green card rules making it harder to plan and underwrite a multi-year horizon,” said Kapil Joshi, chief executive of IT staffing at Quess Corp.Returning to India does not automatically translate into better employment opportunities or higher pay. A recent survey conducted by Blind, an anonymous community app for job seekers, found that several professionals returning from the US were taking up roles in the India offices of the same multinational companies where they had previously worked. However, their salaries were significantly lower.The survey covered 1,276 verified professionals in India. It found that 53% had seen people return from the US because of visa-related problems. Among them, 36% said colleagues or job candidates had already come back, while another 17% knew people who were planning to return.The pressure created by visa rules is also being felt by students. The post-study period available to international students in the UK is being reduced, with the duration of the graduate visa set to fall from two years to 18 months for applications made from January next year.
Article Summary: The UK has tightened its work visa requirements at least twice over the past two years. The minimum salary threshold for positions eligible for a skilled worker visa increased from nearly $35,409 in 2024 to around $52,303 by April, before rising further to nearly $56,358 in July 2025. The trend is also beginning to reflect in the employment market.

Article Title: New costlier iPhones may boost refurbished smartphones' demand
Article Text: NEW DELHI: Apple's latest iPhone launch could trigger a fresh wave of trade-ins, while strengthening demand for older, refurbished models, as sharply higher flagship prices push buyers towards more affordable ways of entering the company's ecosystem, according to Cashify.The refurbished-device platform expects buybacks to increase within 30 days of the launch and gather pace over the following 60-90 days as supplies improve, festive offers expand and more customers upgrade.The iPhone 15 and iPhone 16 series are expected to record the strongest increase in buybacks. The iPhone 13 and 14 could continue contributing substantial volumes because of their larger installed base.Apple accounted for 65.3% of refurbished smartphone sales on its platform in 2025 and 32.6% of all devices bought back. The iPhone 13 was both its bestselling refurbished iPhone and most frequently traded-in model. The iPhone 13 represented 6.93% of Cashify's smartphone buybacks but accounted for 15.5% of refurbished demand, indicating that demand exceeded the volume volume entering its resale system.Meanwhile, refurbished-phone retailers expect demand for older iPhones to strengthen following the latest price increases, particularly among customers who want an Apple device but are unwilling to spend close to Rs 1 lakh on a new base model.Retailers also expect warranties, battery health and device certification to become more important as first-time buyers move towards the secondary market.Higher supplies would ordinarily reduce prices of outgoing models. However, Cashify expects the elevated prices of new iPhones to simultaneously lift demand for previous generations, potentially limiting the correction. Prices could therefore soften gradually instead of declining sharply.Demand is expected to shift progressively towards the iPhone 14 and 15 as availability improves, while the iPhone 16 may initially remain in the premium refurbished category because of its higher residual value.
Article Summary: Apple accounted for 65.3% of refurbished smartphone sales on Cashify's platform in 2025. The iPhone 13 was both its bestselling refurbished iPhone and most frequently traded-in model. Cashify expects the elevated prices of new iPhones to simultaneously lift demand for previous generations, potentially limiting the correction.

Article Title: AB InBev growth in India better than industry: Prez
Article Text: New Delhi: AB InBev, the world's largest brewer, has outpaced India's beer market in the first half of the year, making the country one of Budweiser's top three markets globally in June, behind US and China. The strong double-digit growth came despite the West Asia conflict, which disrupted supply chains and triggered can shortages, as premiumisation emerged as a key driver of beer consumption, Kartikeya Sharma, president, AB InBev India told TOI.Premium beers grew about 20% during Jan-June, buoyed by regulatory changes in key markets, such as Maharashtra and Karnataka, helping the company gain share. While the industry grew around 12%, AB InBev grew faster, cornering about 20% share in the overall beer market of 20 million hectoliters in the first half.The premium segment accounts for about 65% of the company's volumes, with brands including Budweiser, Corona and Hoegaarden key growth drivers.Also, cans are becoming an increasingly important format in India's beer market, driven by convenience and portability, and account for about 28% of the overall beer market. The company's share is at over 40%, reflecting its sharper focus.Further, beer category is thriving particularly in states where taxes have been normalised and there is a level-playing field between beer and spirits, with Maharashtra growing about 40%, he said.As against this, the hard spirits category seems to be declining.Indicating a potential shift to moderation in consumer choice, Karnataka has emerged as a test case with the sale of beer below 5% ABV (alcohol by volume) doubling to 20% in three months. In May, it asked manufacturers to state alcohol content to the first decimal. In other states, beer may simply be categorised as above or below 5% alcohol."That encourages us to innovate around different consumer needs. A consumer may want a mid-week low-ABV beer at 2%, 2.5%, even 0%, depending on occasion. We lead the beer category globally and have examples in many markets where low-ABV products drive participation. Karnataka gives us the ability to test that thesis, and we intend to do so. Favorable policy should ultimately give consumers more choice, more variety, different price points'', Sharma stated."In the future, if there are opportunities, capabilities we want to bring in, or innovations we first want to test through the import route, those could be areas where we benefit,'' he added.
Article Summary: The strong double-digit growth came despite the West Asia conflict, which disrupted supply chains and triggered can shortages.Premium beers grew about 20% during Jan-June, buoyed by regulatory changes in key markets, such as Maharashtra and Karnataka, helping the company gain share.

Article Title: Coforge hires Egon Zehnder to find two ind directors
Article Text: Bengaluru: Coforge has appointed global executive search firm Egon Zehnder to identify two additional independent directors as the company moves to strengthen its board, following the resignations of chairman OP Bhatt and Nomination and Remuneration Committee (NRC) chair DK Singh. The board said the governance issues that led to the exits had no impact on the company's operations, financial reporting or business outlook. Board members also said there was no dissent among them. Independent director Beth Boucher has been appointed NRC chair.Interim chair Vivek Sharma said the search would be global, focusing on candidates with governance experience, professional expertise and strategic perspectives to strengthen the board and support Coforge's long-term growth. Sharma will also oversee the process to elect a permanent chair but said he would not be a candidate for the role.The board detailed the findings of an internal audit that preceded the resignations. KPMG, Coforge's internal auditor, reviewed the accuracy of board reporting as part of its FY27 audit plan. The audit found that board evaluation reports were available only to the then NRC chair and chairman, and were not shared with other board members."The manner in which the evaluation findings were presented without sharing copies of report by chairman of board and NRC chair did not cover all relevant aspects of the findings," said John Speight, president and executive director, in an investor call on Monday.
Article Summary: Coforge has appointed global executive search firm Egon Zehnder to identify two additional independent directors. The board said the governance issues that led to the exits had no impact on the company's operations, financial reporting or business outlook. Board members also said there was no dissent among them.

Article Title: BP looks for bigger play in oil exploration
Article Text: NEW DELHI: BP is looking to widen participation in India's oil and gas exploration sector and is planning to work with partners on new exploration opportunities as govt opens up a larger part of the country's offshore acreage for drilling.BP India chairman Kartikeya Dube told TOI that the company was working with partners to participate in upcoming Open Acreage Licencing Policy (OALP) and Discovered Small Field (DSF) rounds. "I can't answer questions exactly about the future because they are subject to listed company confidentiality. What I can tell you is... we are working with our partners to participate in both of them," Dube said, while declining to give details of future bids.BP has participated with Reliance Industries in DSF round and OALP-10 shallow-water opportunities. It has a partnership with Reliance on east coast and offers technical advisory to ONGC on Mumbai High and Western Offshore.BP's exploration push is alongside its work with ONGC to increase production from mature offshore fields. Dube said the company expects about 60% upside in production at Mumbai High and around 25% at Western Offshore as it works to arrest the decline in output from the fields.BP's technical advisory at the Mumbai High project began in early 2025, while the Western Offshore engagement went live in Aug this year."The way the contracts are organised is (that) every giant field in Mumbai High is about 50 years old. They have a decline and our bit is to basically arrest that decline... to lower the rate of decline," Dube said. "What we have brought is not only technology, which everybody brings, right. But, you have to bring people with the right technical experience. That's what makes a difference."
Article Summary: BP India chairman Kartikeya Dube told TOI that the company was working with partners to participate in upcoming Open Acreage Licencing Policy (OALP) and Discovered Small Field (DSF) rounds. "I can't answer questions exactly about the future because they are subject to listed company confidentiality," he said.

Article Title: Essar arm to buy UK fuel retailer for nearly $550 million
Article Text: NEW DELHI: Essar Energy Transition's retail arm has agreed to acquire independent UK forecourt operator SGN Retail in a deal estimated at about 400 million pounds ($540 million or Rs 5,166 crore), adding 118 sites to its network and creating a 235-site estate as it seeks to build a vertically integrated fuel business in Britain.EET Retail, the retail division of Essar Energy Transition Fuels, in a statement said it had agreed to acquire 100% of SGN Retail, which was founded by Graham Peacock and Susan Tobbell.While the company did not disclose the financial details, sources said the deal is estimated to be about 400 million pounds. The deal will give EET Retail annual fuel throughput of more than 650 million litres, combining SGN Retail's 118 locations with the 117 sites already operated by EET Retail.EET Retail said the enlarged network would make it the UK's second-largest forecourt operator with direct integration into fuel production. It plans to expand the network to about 800 sites by 2031, equivalent to roughly 9% of the UK market, with fuel supplied by Essar's Stanlow refinery in Cheshire."Building a scaled, vertically integrated retail forecourt platform is a critical pillar of our long-term UK strategy.SGN Retail is one of the highest-quality forecourt networks in the UK well ahead of the market. This acquisition accelerates our plan to build a nationwide, vertically integrated platform of 800 sites, backed by direct refinery supply and delivering competitive prices at the pump for UK motorists," said Arvan Ruia, CEO of EET Retail.The acquisition comes as EET seeks to reconnect fuel production with retail distribution, arguing that the UK's fuel market has become increasingly fragmented over the past two decades as oil majors reduced investment in domestic refining.EET said the model would allow fuel refined at Stanlow to be distributed more directly to its own forecourts, reducing reliance on imports and multiple layers in the domestic supply chain. "This is a unique, best-in-class opportunity and advances a core part of our M&A strategy. The transaction is backed by a top-tier group of banks spanning four continents, several supporting the UK forecourt sector for the first time, underscoring confidence in our backward-integrated growth model and in the UK fuels and convenience markets," said Viral Gathani, head of strategic transactions at Essar Energy Transition (EET).The transaction is being financed through a combination of cash and a new 250 million pound senior debt facility arranged by First Abu Dhabi Bank, Macquarie Bank, Mizrahi Tefahot Bank, Natixis, OakNorth Bank, Royal Bank of Canada, and others. Agencies
Article Summary: EET Retail, the retail division of Essar Energy Transition Fuels, in a statement said it had agreed to acquire 100% of SGN Retail. EET Retail said the enlarged network would make it the UK's second-largest forecourt operator with direct integration into fuel production.

Article Title: Amazon's quick commerce business crosses $1 billion in gross annualised sales
Article Text: MUMBAI: Amazon's quick commerce business has now crossed $1 billion in gross annualised sales in India over the past three-month period and has caught up with competition to become one of the top three market players in Delhi and Bengaluru, despite a late entry into the instant delivery space, a top company executive said.In an interview, Amazon's India country manager Samir Kumar said the growth has come on the back of orders doubling every quarter. A big push has also come from Prime customers, who end up shopping about three times more on Amazon Now. "Prime is a big driver for our flywheel but even non-prime customers are coming in quite a good number. As we start reaching smaller cities, we are also seeing a very, very healthy growth in non-Prime customers. They are also converting to Prime," Kumar said.Gross annualised sales is typically calculated by taking the total gross sales for a month or a quarter and multiplying it to project a full 12-month period. It reflects the value of orders placed minus discounts, cancellations and excluding GST.Amazon Now officially started operations in March quarter last year, about four months after launch of Flipkart's Minutes and having ceded much of the market share to Eternal's Blinkit, Swiggy's Instamart and Zepto.In what seems as a clear mandate from Amazon's Seattle headquarters to scale up Now's execution on ground here, the firm's top boss Andy Jassy on a visit to India earlier this year said Now will expand to over 300 cities and build the largest delivery-in-minutes network. It was Jassy's first India tour since assuming office in 2021. By Diwali, Now will be scaled to 100 cities and to 1,000 dark stores by year-end. Sources said Now's orders stand at about 700,000 per day. In all, it has gained market share of about 10% by orders and about 14% by value."Our growth engine is still going to be a lot more penetrating into smaller cities and towns," Kumar said. About 70% of Amazon's (overall) customers come from smaller cities. The company has taken Now to cities such as Udupi, Warangal, Guntur and plans are afoot to launch it in places like Kapurthala and Gurdaspur going ahead. Now will have a play across both mass and premium price points and Kumar's target is to widen the selection of products and categories on the platform. "Our focus will be on whether we can serve a customer need in minutes in a sustainable and safe way," Kumar said.
Article Summary: Amazon's India country manager Samir Kumar said the growth has come on the back of orders doubling every quarter. A big push has also come from Prime customers, who end up shopping about three times more on Amazon Now. Sources said Now's orders stand at about 700,000 per day.

Article Title: Solar Industries acquires S African company for 13,000 crore
Article Text:
To get a foothold in farm sector

Nagpur: Solar Industries, a Nagpur-headquartered explosives manufacturer, has signed a definitive agreement to take over South Africa's Omnia Holdings in a Rs 12,951 crore deal, leading to formation of one of the world's largest and most integrated blasting solutions platform.Solar would also get access to key international markets, including US, Canada, Australia, Brazil and Indonesia, apart from southern and western Africa through Omnia's network. The buyout will enable Solar Group to get a foothold in the farm sector too. Omnia is a major manufacturer of ammonium nitrate, which is used in agriculture and explosives sectors.The buyout is expected to be completed in early-to mid-2027, subject to customary conditions, including competition approvals in relevant jurisdictions. After completion, Omnia will be delisted from Johannesburg Stock Exchange and A2X Markets, the company said in a regulatory filing. The proposed transaction marks a transformational milestone in Solar Group's strategic ambition to become leading global explosives and mining solutions provider, the company said.Johannesburg-based Omnia operates in 23 countries, while it reaches out to 40 nations through a network of 70 distribution centres, clocking a turnover of $1.4 billion (Rs 13,307 crore) for the fiscal ending March 2026, compared with $1.3 billion in FY25 and $1.2 billion in FY24, and has remained cash positive, stated a Solar Group representative.The buyout will take place through Solar SA Investments Proprietary, a wholly owned subsidiary of Solar Industries. This is the second South African takeover by Solar Group in the recent past. In 2024, it acquired ProBlast, a local South African company specialising in open cast mining, drilling, blasting and explosive services. Omnia's agriculture segment operates nitric acid and ammonium nitrate production facilities, which are the largest and most reliable in the region, said a note."Omnia is a business we long admired for the strength of its mining and agriculture businesses' differentiated technology, brands and deep customer relationships. The proposed transaction marks an important milestone in our ambition to become a global leader in explosives and blasting solutions, while providing us a meaningful entry into the integrated crop nutrition and biological solutions," said Solar Group's MD Manish Nuwal.Omnia's BME brand brings a strong international mining platform, high-quality assets, technological leadership in electronic initiation and integrated ammonium nitrate manufacturing facility, said Nuwal. Solar Group has steadily expanded its footprint across Africa. It first entered the South African Development Community (SDAC) region in 2010 by establishing a manufacturing facility at Zambia in 2010.
Article Summary: Solar Industries, a Nagpur-headquartered explosives manufacturer, has signed a definitive agreement to take over South Africa's Omnia Holdings. The buyout will enable Solar Group to get a foothold in the farm sector too. Omnia is a major manufacturer of ammonium nitrate, which is used in agriculture and explosives sectors.

Article Title: Retail inflation surges to 8-month high of 4.8% in August
Article Text:
Factory gate inflation rises faster

NEW DELHI: Retail inflation based on the consumer price index (CPI) hit an eight-month high of 4.8% (y-o-y) in Aug from 4.5% in July, driven largely by higher food prices, NSO (National Statistics Office) data released Monday showed.At current level it is above RBI 's 4% target for the third consecutive month, although it remains within the 2-6% comfort zone. Separately, wholesale price index (WPI) data pegged factory gate inflation at 9.9% in Aug, from 9.8% in July, on the back of higher fuel and manufactured goods prices.NSO data estimated that food inflation accelerated to 6% in Aug, compared to 5.5% in July. The impact of fresh hostilities in West Asia, which has increased oil prices, was seen in sectors, such as transport and restaurants. Prices in restaurants services accelerated 8.4% in Aug compared to 7.7% in July, while inflation in transport services was at 4.6% against 4.4%.Retail inflation remained stronger in rural India (5.2%), up from 4.8% in July. Urban inflation, too, witnessed a rise to 4.3% from 4%. The latest retail inflation data assumes significance as RBI's monetary policy committee (MPC) is due to meet early next month."The inflation outlook remains vulnerable to both external and weather-related risks.Uncertainty surrounding transit through the Strait of Hormuz continues to pose upside risks to global energy prices. Domestically, below-normal rainfall remains a key concern... A sustained uptick in inflation could strengthen the case for a rate hike in the coming months. The Oct RBI policy decision will be crucial to watch, especially as some major central banks have already embarked on a rate-hiking cycle," said Rajni Sinha, chief economist at CareEdge.ICRA chief economist Aditi Nayar earlier expected a rate hike in Dec. "If crude prices remain elevated in the run up to the upcoming MPC meeting, hinting at an impending upward revision in the Retail Selling Prices (RSP) of petrol and diesel, which could percolate into generalised price pressures, then the expected rate hike could get pre-poned to Oct 2026 from Dec 2026."
Article Summary: Retail inflation based on the consumer price index (CPI) hit an eight-month high of 4.8% (y-o-y) in Aug from 4.5% in July. At current level it is above RBI's 4% target for the third consecutive month, although it remains within the 2-6% comfort zone. The impact of fresh hostilities in West Asia, which has increased oil prices, was seen in sectors like transport and restaurants.

Article Title: National Engineers' Day 2026: Meet A. Lalitha, India’s first female engineer who defied a male-dominated profession
Article Text:
A Lalitha, India’s first female engineer, broke barriers by pursuing engineering while raising her daughter as a young widow. (Image credits- All Together)

A young mother who refused to give up on education

She entered a college filled with men and etched her name on the leaves of history

From railway workshops to major engineering projects

Lalitha’s work on Bhakra Nangal Dam

She took India’s women engineers to the global stage

A legacy that began with one woman refusing to step back

Engineering has always been connected with males and has remained a male-dominated segment. Remember that dialogue from 3 Idiots? “Beta hua to engineer aur beti hui to doctor.” No matter how much we preach about gender equality, deep down, we have all witnessed the ever-existent and deeply rooted patriarchy that our society carries forth. But we are saying this in 2026. And a girl in the 1900s unshackled all the barriers and chose an unconventional path. Ayyalasomayajula Lalitha, born in 1919 in Madras, etched her name as one of the first female engineers of India.As it is well said by some, “We think it to be impossible until it is made possible by someone.” And hence, we always owe these trailblazers a lot. They opened the doors and left the footprints for their predecessors to follow. Lalitha’s journey was not an aisle of roses; it was filled with personal loss, determination, and an unshakable commitment to education. But her story is not merely about being the first woman to earn an engineering degree in India. It is about how she opened a door that had barely existed for women.A Lalitha was born on August 27, 1919, into a Telugu-speaking family in Madras, now Chennai. She was married at the age of 15 and gave birth to her daughter, Syamala, in 1937.Just four months after her daughter’s birth, Lalitha lost her husband. At an age when her life could easily have been defined by circumstance, Lalitha chose education instead. With the support of her father, Pappu Subba Rao, who was himself a professor at the College of Engineering, Guindy, she completed her secondary education and decided to pursue engineering. At that time, engineering colleges in India were overwhelmingly male-dominated.Lalitha joined the College of Engineering, Guindy, to study electrical engineering. She was the only woman among hundreds of male students.Yet, according to her daughter, the environment at the college was more supportive than one might expect. The administration arranged separate hostel accommodation for Lalitha, while fellow students ensured that she did not feel isolated.Lalitha was not entirely alone in breaking the gender barrier. P.K. Thressia and Leelamma Koshie, née George, were also studying engineering at the institution around the same period.In 1943, Lalitha graduated with a degree in electrical engineering, becoming India’s first woman engineer.Her education did not end with a degree. She undertook a one-year apprenticeship at the Jamalpur Railway Workshop, gaining practical exposure to engineering work in one of the country’s major railway repair and overhaul facilities.After completing her training, Lalitha worked with the Central Standards Organisation in Shimla. She also assisted her father with research involving smokeless ovens and an electrical musical instrument known as the jelectromonium.She subsequently spent a year in the electrical department of the East Indian Railways before joining the Indian government's Office of the Electrical Commissioner as a technical assistant.In 1948, she took another major step in her career when she joined Associated Electrical Industries (AEI), a British engineering firm in Calcutta.Her work there would place her on one of independent India’s most ambitious infrastructure projects.At AEI, Lalitha worked on the Bhakra Nangal Dam project, one of the country's landmark engineering undertakings.Her responsibilities included designing transmission lines and substation layouts. The work demanded technical expertise at a time when women engineers were still an extreme rarity in India.She remained associated with AEI, which was later taken over by the General Electric Company, for nearly three decades. She retired in 1977 after a long professional career.For Lalitha, engineering was not simply a profession through which she had broken a gender barrier. It became a field in which she built a sustained body of work.Lalitha's contribution extended beyond her professional assignments.In 1953, the Council of the Institution of Electrical Engineers in London elected her as an associate member. She was later promoted to full membership in 1966.In 1964, she became the only female engineer from India to attend the First International Conference of Women Engineers and Scientists in New York.The following year, she was elected a member of the British Women's Engineering Society.Her international engagement also had a wider purpose. As India's representative on the organising committee for the Second International Conference of Women Engineers and Scientists, held in Cambridge in 1967, Lalitha helped ensure that five Indian women were able to attend the conference.Her achievement, therefore, was not confined to becoming the first. She also worked to make sure that more women could follow.Lalitha never remarried after her husband's death. Her sister-in-law helped raise her daughter, Syamala, who later earned degrees in science and became a mathematics teacher.Lalitha died on October 12, 1979, at the age of 60 after suffering a brain aneurysm. But she left this abode, leaving an indelible mark on the hearts of young generations. Her story inherently carries forth not only a powerful lesson but also an emotion that being first is pivotal, but making the path easier for those who will follow is a greater achievement. Today, on National Engineers' Day, let us remember and pay our tributes to all those ingenous minds who walked with a beacon of light and knocked on the doors that were otherwise closed.
Article Summary: Ayyalasomayajula Lalitha, born in 1919 in Madras, etched her name as one of the first female engineers of India. She was married at the age of 15 and gave birth to her daughter, Syamala, in 1937. At that time, engineering colleges in India were overwhelmingly male-dominated. Her education did not end with a degree. She undertook a one-year apprenticeship at the Jamalpur Railway Workshop, gaining practical exposure to engineering.

Article Title: Global AI stocks slide as warnings over rapid development trigger investor concerns
Article Text:
AI stocks tumble as debt, valuations and slowing development fears hit market (representative image)

Amodei calls for slower AI development

AI investment faces fresh questions

Investors remain divided

AI-linked stocks across global markets plunged on Monday after leaders of some of the world’s biggest artificial intelligence companies called for a slower pace of development, raising fresh questions over the huge investments that have driven the sector’s rally.The warnings from Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, backed by OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and xAI chief Elon Musk, added to scrutiny of an AI industry that is increasingly relying on debt and circular financing while raising spending forecasts.Nasdaq e-mini futures fell 1.9%, with chip stocks among the biggest decliners. Nvidia fell 3%, Advanced Micro Devices dropped 5.7% and SpaceX fell 2.6%. Meta and Amazon declined more than 1.4% each.In Europe, technology stocks fell 2.5%, with chip equipment maker ASML down 5.8%, Infineon falling 8.4% and Siemens Energy losing 7.4%.Asian AI-linked stocks also came under pressure. SoftBank fell as much as 13.2%, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company declined 1.2% and South Korea’s SK Hynix dropped 6.3%.Amodei, in an essay shared on X on Saturday, called on AI companies to slow the pace at which they improve the capabilities of their models, citing growing concerns over potential misuse and the difficulty of controlling increasingly powerful systems.He warned that within six to 12 months, AI agents “could be capable of taking over the entire internet potentially causing hundreds of billions of dollars in damage.”Anthropic had also released a threat intelligence report detailing the use of its Claude AI models in activities ranging from weapons development and cyber operations to surveillance and fraud.OpenAI researcher Jacob Coxon subsequently resigned, saying the companies developing frontier AI were moving too quickly.“The people building AI earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade,” Coxon said.Altman has backed Amodei’s call for greater caution, while also confirming that OpenAI would not proceed with an initial public offering this year, citing safety concerns. He said the risks of human extinction posed by AI were “unacceptable”.Musk also endorsed Amodei’s position, writing: “Dario is right.”The warnings have raised concerns about whether the extraordinary spending on AI infrastructure can continue if the pace of technological development slows.“If the AI race slows materially, the key question becomes: who pays for all that infrastructure?” said Ipek Ozkardeskaya, senior analyst at Swissquote.“The leases, debt and power commitments remain even if expected compute demand and revenue growth slow. And that could bring credit risk increasingly into the AI story,” she added.AI-related stocks have powered a significant part of global equity gains since OpenAI launched ChatGPT in 2022. However, concerns over cyberattacks involving AI agents and public opposition to data-centre construction have added to scrutiny of the industry.Despite the latest warnings, Morgan Stanley’s Brian Nowak expects AI spending to exceed $1.2 trillion by 2027.Deutsche Bank said the competitive race between companies and countries remained intense and that it was difficult to imagine firms voluntarily slowing down while rivals continued to advance.Some investors dismissed the warnings. Michael Burry, known for betting against the US housing market before the 2008 financial crisis, described the warnings as “hype and puffery” and “cover for real uncontrollable slowing growth”.Others said the warnings could still weigh on AI and semiconductor stocks in the short term because valuations depend on strong demand and continued technological progress.“Their valuations assume both strong demand and a relentless pace of technological progress,” said Charu Chanana, chief investment strategist at Saxo Bank in Singapore, as quoted by Reuters.“When expectations are this high, even a possible delay can trigger profit-taking.”The market sell-off also came as oil prices rose amid concerns over global energy supplies.Brent crude rose more than 3% to around $108.74 a barrel after Saudi Arabia shut a major oil pipeline following an attack.US markets were also facing pressure from higher energy prices and rising Treasury yields, while investors were monitoring the Federal Reserve’s upcoming policy meeting.Meanwhile, the US and Chinese governments are expected to hold AI safety talks this month as part of broader bilateral discussions, according to two people briefed on the plans.
Article Summary: Nasdaq e-mini futures fell 1.9%, with chip stocks among the biggest decliners. Nvidia fell 3%, Advanced Micro Devices dropped 5.7% and SpaceX fell 2.6%. Meta and Amazon declined more than 1.4% each.

Article Title: Oil prices jump over 2%: Brent tops $107 as fresh Saudi, Strait of Hormuz strikes fuel supply fears
Article Text:
Brent crude climbs.

Oil prices rose more than 2% on Monday as fresh Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and Iranian strikes on vessels in the Gulf added to supply concerns following the shutdown of a key Saudi oil pipeline.Brent crude futures rose $2.90, or 2.77%, to $107.51 a barrel by 2313 GMT. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude gained $2.27, or 2.27%, to $102.32 a barrel.Prices had initially climbed more than 3% at the market open. Brent rose $3.62, or 3.46%, to $108.23 a barrel by 2214 GMT on Sunday, while WTI increased $3.15, or 3.15%, to $103.20 a barrel.Saudi state media on Sunday released footage showing damage to homes and a mosque in the southern Jazan province following what it described as a Houthi attack. The Iran-aligned Houthis also said they had targeted a Saudi military base in a neighbouring province.Separately, a vessel in the Strait of Hormuz was struck by a projectile, causing a fire and forcing its crew to evacuate, the British maritime security agency UKMTO said.Iran said one person was killed and four crew members were wounded after an Iranian commercial vessel was struck off the country’s coast.Oil prices were expected to rise after Saudi Arabia’s East-West oil pipeline was shut on Friday following a drone attack originating in Iraq.The pipeline allows Saudi Arabia, the world’s largest oil exporter, to reroute shipments and avoid the Strait of Hormuz. Its shutdown threatens up to 4% of global oil supply.Meanwhile, Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthis reached the strategic island of Perim on Friday, tightening their position near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, another key oil transit route that has carried 4-5% of global supply in recent months.Oil prices have risen around 8% over the past week, crossing $100 a barrel for the first time since July, as escalating tensions in the Middle East raised concerns over global supplies.The Strait of Hormuz remained at the centre of the confrontation. Nearly one-fifth of the world’s oil passed through the strategic waterway before the war began, with both the United States and Iran seeking to exert control over it.Oman postponed a scheduled meeting with Iran and other regional countries on Monday to discuss the management of shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.Omani foreign minister Badr Albusaidi said on X that the meeting had been postponed “in the interests of consensus”. Mohammad Ali Bak, an official in Iran’s foreign ministry quoted by IRNA, said the talks were postponed “at the request of some regional countries”.The meeting was expected to focus on efforts by Iran and Oman, which lies on the other side of the strait, to manage shipping through the key waterway.No peace talks have taken place in the war, which began six months ago with US and Israeli strikes, since an interim agreement reached in June collapsed after a few weeks.
Article Summary: Brent crude futures rose $2.90, or 2.77%, to $107.51 a barrel by 2313 GMT. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude gained 2.27% to $102.32 a barrel. Prices had initially climbed more than 3% at the market open.

Article Title: US should have the world's lowest interest rate: Trump
Article Text:
US President Donald Trump

No country in the world should have lower interest rates than US, President Donald Trump said on Sunday, days before Federal Reserve's next policy meeting.Speaking to reporters at the Irish Open golf tournament, Trump said he did not know whether Fed policy makers will raise interest rates at their meeting this week. But he argued that US "should be paying the lowest interest rate in the world" no matter what Federal Reserve's data indicates about inflation and the economy.The Fed meeting will take place less than a week after a key measure of underlying inflation, Labor Department's Consumer Price Index, on Friday posted its largest increase in four months. That reinforced expectations that the US central bank will raise rates.The central bank's governors are meeting just weeks before the midterm elections that will determine whether Republicans keep their slim majorities in both chambers of US Congress. A rate hike could add to voter concerns about affordability, according to recent Reuters/Ipsos polls.Trump's approval ratings have fallen as inflation has persisted. He has argued that Fed's interest rate levels have helped other countries at the expense of the US. "I know more about formulas than anybody, and with the best credit in the world, we make other countries rich," Trump said on Sunday.
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump says no country in the world should have lower interest rates than US. Trump said he did not know whether Fed policy makers will raise interest rates at their meeting this week. The Fed meeting will take place less than a week after a key measure of underlying inflation posted its largest increase in four months.

Article Title: Oil infra hit by Ukraine, Russia gets 70% of its fuel from India
Article Text: NEW DELHI: As Russian refineries came under attack from Ukraine, damaging energy infrastructure and crippling domestic fuel supplies, Moscow imported a record 172,000 tonnes of oil products in Aug, with nearly 70% of it coming from India, Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA) has said in its monthly report.India, however, remained the second-largest importer of crude oil from Russia in Aug, behind only China, though its imports decreased compared with the previous two months.According to the report, India's exports to Moscow included 1,20,000 tonnes of gasoline (petrol) worth 78 million euros, refined from Russian crude at a refinery in India partly owned by Russia's Rosneft."Russia's import volumes in Aug 2026 were more than seven times the previous monthly high recorded since the full-scale invasion (of Ukraine) and three times the total import volume for the whole of 2025," CREA said in its analysis of Russian fossil fuel exports and sanctions for Aug.The report added that all the gasoline was loaded at Gujarat's Vadinar refinery and sold by EU-sanctioned Nayara Energy to Rosneft. Rosneft holds 49.1% of Nayara Energy, while Vadinar got 100% of its crude from Russia in the first eight months of 2026, up from 81% across 2025. "Russia is therefore paying a refinery that it partly owns to process its own crude into fuel it can no longer produce domestically, before shipping it back halfway around the world," the report stated.CREA said each cargo of gasoline exported from Vadinar to Russia was transferred between vessels in a ship-to-ship operation off Egypt before being unloaded at Russia's Arctic port of Beloe More.One of the largest exporters of refined petroleum products, Russia has seen its gasoline imports surge recently. Compared with 6% on aver-age between 2023 and 2025, gasoline imports accounted for 74% of its total oil-product imports in Aug. South Korea and Egypt also exported to Russia.Of the 4.8 billion euros of hydrocarbons imported by India from Russia in Aug, crude oil accounted for 4.1 billion euros, or 87%, CREA said. Indian imports of Russian crude, however, fell 24% from July after reaching record levels in the previous two months.
Article Summary: Russia imported a record 172,000 tonnes of oil products in Aug, with nearly 70% of it coming from India. India, however, remained the second-largest importer of crude oil from Russia, behind only China. India's exports to Moscow included 1,20,000 tons of gasoline (petrol) refined from Russian crude.

Article Title: 'Canada wants it very badly': Trump on trade deal with Ottawa, says it'll be 'fairly soon'
Article Text:
US President Donald Trump during a meeting with Ireland's Prime Minister Micheál Martin at Farmleigh House in Dublin

US President Donald Trump on Saturday claimed that Canada was keen to reach a trade deal with the United States and that an agreement could come “fairly soon”.“Canada wants to make a deal very badly,” Trump told reporters after meeting Irish Prime Minister Micheál Martin in Dublin.“Canada has to treat our farmers better. They can't charge our farmers tariffs,” he said, adding, “You'll probably see a deal with Canada fairly soon.”Trump's comments came during a two-day visit to Ireland that has combined political engagements with a stop at his golf resort in Doonbeg, where he is attending the Irish Open. He also met Irish President Catherine Connolly in Dublin.The Canada remarks come amid an escalating trade dispute between Washington and Ottawa. The US Trade Representative said this week that Canada had walked away from what Washington described as a near-final trade deal and announced further measures targeting certain Canadian products.Trump also drew attention during his Dublin visit by saying he would “love” to see Ireland unified, adding that he believed it would happen eventually and would be a “fantastic thing”. His remarks prompted a sharp response from pro-British unionists in Northern Ireland.“Well, I don't want to cause any problems, but I will tell you, I'd love to see it unified,” Trump said alongside Martin. “It's going to happen eventually ... I think it would be a fantastic thing.”Trump later described Irish reunification as a “very cool thing”, while acknowledging that the UK would have a say. Under the 1998 Good Friday Agreement, a referendum on Northern Ireland's constitutional status can be called by the British government under specified conditions.The remarks marked a departure from the traditionally cautious US position on Irish reunification. The US played a key role in the peace process that culminated in the 1998 agreement.Trump joked about the concentration of US medical companies in Ireland, saying, “You took all our medical companies, we've got to get a couple of them back.”“You fleeced us but that's okay... There's a lot of room to go around and our relationship with you is fantastic,” Trump said.Trump is due to attend the Irish Open at his Doonbeg resort later in his visit. The trip has also drawn protests in Dublin and western Ireland, with Irish authorities mounting a major security operation around the president's movements.
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump claims that Canada is keen to reach a trade deal with the United States. Trump's comments came during a two-day visit to Ireland that has combined political engagements with a stop at his golf resort in Doonbeg. Trump also drew attention during his Dublin visit by saying he would “love” to see Ireland unified.

Article Title: Nvidia weighs $10 billion investment in Anthropic’s mega IPO: Report
Article Text:
Anthropic plans massive IPO

Nvidia and Anthropic's growing ties

Amazon and Google are also major backers

From $965 billion to a possible $2 trillion

Anthropic is planning what could be the biggest IPO in history, with the artificial intelligence giant looking to raise as much as $100 billion at a valuation of around $2 trillion. Nvidia is in talks to become a major early investor in the offering, according to two people familiar with the matter cited by Reuters.Nvidia is considering putting up to $10 billion into the IPO, one of the people said. The talks are still going on and the plans could change, the sources said. They requested anonymity because the discussions are private.If the deal goes ahead, Nvidia would become an early investor in what could be the biggest IPO ever. Its involvement could also strengthen the close business relationship between Nvidia and Anthropic, one of the chipmaker's major customers.Nvidia's possible investment comes as Anthropic depends heavily on Nvidia's chips to run its AI models. At the same time, Anthropic is looking for other chip suppliers as rising demand for Claude has put pressure on its available computing capacity.Nvidia had already said in November 2025 that it would invest up to $10 billion in Anthropic as part of a wider partnership.Under the deal, Anthropic agreed to buy $30 billion of Microsoft Azure computing capacity powered by Nvidia chips.Anchor investors usually agree to buy a fixed amount of shares before an IPO is offered to the wider market. Their early investment can give other investors confidence in the listing.Large IPOs have increasingly looked for such early investors because of the huge amounts of money they are trying to raise. Nvidia and Amazon were among the anchor investors in chip designer Arm's IPO, while Saudi Arabia's PIF was among the anchor investors for SpaceX.Anthropic already has some of the world's biggest technology companies as investors. Amazon and Google are also among its major suppliers of computing power.In April, Anthropic said it would commit more than $100 billion over 10 years to Amazon's AWS while using more than 1 million of Amazon's Trainium2 chips. It has also agreed with Google and Broadcom to add several gigawatts of TPU capacity.The company is trying to get access to more computing power as its revenue has grown sharply. It is also building an in-house team to design its own chips for Claude, with the aim of having greater control over its hardware costs.The proposed IPO would mark another big jump in Anthropic's valuation.The Claude maker raised $65 billion in May at a post-money valuation of $965 billion. Its annualised revenue run rate had crossed $65 billion by the end of July, compared with about $9 billion at the end of 2025, according to the company.The possible $2 trillion valuation also depends partly on Anthropic's projections of around $190 billion to $200 billion in revenue in 2028, Reuters previously reported.The listing is expected to be completed before the US midterm elections in November.An Anthropic listing would add to a series of major IPOs that have helped push the US market towards a record year. Elon Musk's SpaceX made its debut in June.US IPOs, excluding special-purpose acquisition companies, raised a record $137 billion through the end of August, according to Dealogic.
Article Summary: Anthropic is planning what could be the biggest IPO in history. It is looking to raise as much as $100 billion at a valuation of around $2 trillion. Nvidia is in talks to become a major early investor in the offering.

Article Title: Ice cream to defence: How Canada’s tariff war with US is boosting local businesses
Article Text:
Canada’s tariff war with US is boosting local businesses

Local products in the basket

‘Buy Canadian’ gets a boost

Defence firms look beyond the US

Others face price pressure

The US and Canada are embroiled in a tariff war, and it may “will come at a cost” for Ottawa as the Canadian PM Mark Carney had warned. But the fight is proving a win for at rather unusual sectors: from the ice-cream counter and gift shops to wineries and even defence manufacturing.As American goods face fresh Canadian tariffs, local businesses have seen an uptick due to the “buy Canadian” wave.Prime Minister Mark Carney has warned that moving away from the US as Canada’s biggest trading partner “will come at a cost,” adding that the counter-tariffs on American goods “are necessary to protect our workers”.The new Canadian levies cover nearly C$28 billion ($20 billion) of American products, ranging from steel and furniture to cotton T-shirts, with tariffs as high as 50%.For Chapman’s, Canada’s largest independent ice cream manufacturer, the trade tensions have coincided with some of its best summer sales.The family-run company employs 1,150 people in Markdale, Ontario, about two hours north-west of Toronto. Ashley Chapman, the company’s chief operating officer, said the business had benefited as Canadians turned towards local products.“Every time Trump insults Canada, Canadians buy more Canadian things,” Ashley Chapman, chief operating officer for Chapman’s ice cream told the Financial Times.“It actually has worked out quite well for us.”The company has also been changing where it gets its ingredients and components. Since March last year, when Trump launched his first round of tariffs on Canada, it has been looking for suppliers outside the US.More than 70% of its American ingredients and components are expected to be replaced with Canadian or non-US sources by mid-2027.“If you had asked me two years ago, ‘what about sourcing your almonds from Australia?’ [instead of the US] I would have said you were insane,” he said.“It’s no great surprise that Trump is pushing for more concessions, more everything. But certainly Canadians have had enough,” he said. “The buy Canadian movement is strong and getting stronger.”Ottawa-based Maker House, a retail and online gift store, has spent the past 18 months selling 300 Canadian-made products. The business also stopped sending products to the US after tariffs increased its costs.“We had a really good year last year and then I think this past week we’ve had a good lift for sure,” said owner Gareth Davies.Among its most popular products were items carrying the slogan “elbows up”, Prime Minister Mark Carney’s battle cry for resisting Trump’s hostility towards Canada.“Everything in the store is made in Canada, you don’t need to worry and check the labels,” Davies said.“All this is a reminder that we can do better to protect our own economy by supporting Canadians who are making things,” he said.The shift has also been felt in Ontario’s wine industry.When American alcohol was taken off the shelves of Ontario’s government-run alcohol stores in response to Trump’s March 2025 tariffs, local producers saw a “significant boost” in demand as consumers embraced the ‘buy local’ sentiment.At Leaning Post Wines in Niagara, near Lake Ontario, sales increased by 3,000 cases.“We saw an additional 3,000 cases of wine sold. When you only make 8,000 cases, that’s a significant increase,” said Nadia Senchuk who runs Leaning Post Wines with her husband Ilya in Niagara, near Lake Ontario.“Our growth was great over the past 18 months,” she said.Ontario has nearly 200 wineries, which contribute more than C$5.5bn to the Canadian economy each year and employ 22,000 people, according to the Vintners Quality Alliance, a trade group. Sales of VQA wine were up 10% year on year last year.The change in trade ties is also creating opportunities for Canadian manufacturers supplying defence-related products.Ontario-based Wuxly began by making coats for Canada’s freezing winters. It now produces defence- and aerospace-grade clothing for a number of military forces around the world.Its workforce of operating seamsters and seamstresses grew from 50 in 2024 to 200 in 2025. The company expects that number to cross 350 by the end of this year.Wuxly is hoping to benefit from greater local procurement in Canadian defence spending, replacing some demand for US suppliers.“We’ve definitely seen more interest in Canadian-made defence textiles under the Build–Partner–Buy framework set out in the defence industrial strategy,” said James Yurichuk, Wuxly’s founder and CEO.The company has also been looking towards Europe as Canada pivots away from US markets. It sent more than 250,000 Canadian-made goods to the EU last year and was “tracking to surpass this number” in 2026.“Perhaps the biggest silver lining of the trade war, and of the broader cooling in relations with the US, has been the heightened interest from European Nato nations,” Yurichuk said.“There’s still real work to do in supporting domestic champions but we’re heading in the right direction,” he added.However, every business is finding the shift easy. Joey Walsh, owner of HockeyStickMan, a hockey equipment retailer, told FT that almost half of the company’s sales had previously come from the US.The family business operates stores in Toronto and Belleville in eastern Ontario and employs around 80 people.
